facts.statement: Mononykus was a small theropod dinosaur measuring between 1 and 1.2 meters in length and weighing 3.5 kilograms.
facts.quote: Mononykus was a very small theropod, estimated around 1 to 1.2 m in length with a weight of 3.5 kg.

facts.statement: Mononykus lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now Mongolia, specifically within the Nemegt Formation.
facts.quote: Mononykus ( , sometimes ; meaning "one claw") is a genus of alvarezsaurid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in what is now Mongolia, specifically the Nemegt Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Mononykus was collected in 1987 from the Bügiin Tsav locality in the Gobi Desert.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, catalog number MPC-D 107/6 (formerly IGM 107/6), was collected in 1987 from the Bügiin Tsav locality of the Nemegt Formation, Gobi Desert.

facts.statement: A new specimen of Mononykus was referred to the genus by Sungjin Lee and colleagues in 2019.
facts.quote: In 2019, Sungjin Lee and colleagues referred a new specimen from the Nemegt Formation, MPC-D 100/206.

facts.statement: A specimen consisting of seven tail vertebrae and a partial hindlimb was discovered in 2008 by the Korea-Mongolia International Dinosaur Expedition.
facts.quote: This specimen consists of seven caudal vertebrae with a partial left hindlimb, and was discovered on a low slope of the Altan Uul III locality in 2008 by an international team of the Korea-Mongolia International Dinosaur Expedition (KID).

facts.statement: Mononykus was originally named Mononychus in 1993 but was renamed that same year because the name was already taken by a beetle.
facts.quote: Mononykus was originally named Mononychus in 1993, but later that year, it was renamed because the original name had already been used for a beetle named by Johann Schueppel, a German entomologist.

facts.statement: Mononykus possessed fused wrist bones similar to birds and a keeled breastbone.
facts.quote: Other characteristics include fused wrist bones similar to those of birds, and a keeled breastbone.

facts.statement: The inner ear structures of Mononykus closely resemble those of barn owls.
facts.quote: The inner ear structures of Mononykus and its relatives closely resembles those of barn owls.

facts.statement: Mononykus was a small, two-legged runner with a single finger ending in a long claw and was likely covered in feathers.
facts.quote: Fue un pequeño dinosaurio bípedo corredor, con un único dedo en las manos, acabado en una larga garra, y probablemente cubierto de plumas.

facts.statement: Mononykus measured approximately 1 meter in length and weighed 3 kilograms.
facts.quote: Mononykus medía aproximadamente 1 metro de largo y 3 kilogramos de peso.

facts.statement: Mononykus had a small skull with small, pointed teeth, suggesting it ate insects and small animals like lizards and mammals.
facts.quote: Tenía un pequeño cráneo, y sus dientes eran pequeños y acentuados, sugiriendo que comía insectos y pequeños animales, tales como lagartos y mamíferos.

facts.statement: Mononykus had strange, stout forearms with a large claw measuring 7.5 centimeters in length, which is the source of its name.
facts.quote: Mononykus tenía antebrazos muy extraños, rechonchos con una garra grande de 7,5 centímetros de largo, de donde proviene su nombre.

facts.statement: The purpose of Mononykus's specialized arms remains a mystery, though some scientists suggest they were used to break open termite mounds, implying an insect-based diet.
facts.quote: El propósito de estos brazos sumamente especializados sigue siendo un misterio, pero algunos científicos han sugerido que los utilizaron para romper los termiteros, como los osos hormigueros modernos, y por lo tanto es posible que se alimentaran sobre todo de insectos.

facts.statement: A layer of soft or "filoplume" feathers may have provided Mononykus with insulation against cold desert nights and served as camouflage.
facts.quote: Una capa de plumas suaves o de "protoplumas pilosas" también puede ser compatibles con la forma de vida que se presume para Mononykus, estas habrían provisto del aislamiento durante las frías noches del desierto y los meses más fríos, además de servirle de camuflaje.

facts.statement: Longer or colored feathers, such as those on the tail, may have been used for courtship displays.
facts.quote: Unas plumas más largas o coloridas, por ejemplo en la cola, podrían haberse utilizado en el cortejo.

facts.statement: Many artistic reconstructions and museum skeletons labeled as Mononykus are actually based on the related genus Shuvuuia.
facts.quote: Because of this, many reconstructions of Mononykus in art and mounted skeletons in museums are in fact based mainly on Shuvuuia.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen IGM N107/6 was discovered in 1987 in the Nemegt Formation of Mongolia.
facts.quote: El holotipo IGM N107/6 fue descubierto en 1987 en la Formación Nemegt, en Mongolia

facts.statement: Mononykus was first briefly described by Perle and colleagues in 1993 and described in more detail in 1994.
facts.quote: descrito brevemente por Perle et al. en 1993 y con más detalle en 1994

facts.statement: In 1993 researchers assigned specimen IGM 100/99 to Mononykus, but later expressed doubts about this assignment in 1994.
facts.quote: En el trabajo de 1993 refirieron a IGM 100/99 a Mononykus, aunque en 1994 expresó dudas sobre esta asignación

facts.statement: Mononykus is currently represented by a single specimen, the holotype.
facts.quote: Mononykus está actualmente representado por un solo ejemplar, el holotipo

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton lacking a tail and containing only small fragments of the skull, including the complete braincase.
facts.quote: Este espécimen consiste en un esqueleto parcial que carece de cola y solo pequeños fragmentos de huesos del cráneo, incluida la caja cerebral completa

facts.statement: Specimens previously assigned to Mononykus were later reassigned to the new genus Shuvuuia by Chiappe and colleagues in 1998.
facts.quote: posteriormente estos e IGM 100/99 fueron todos asignados al nuevo género Shuvuuia por Chiappe et al. en 1998

facts.statement: Specimen IGM 100/99 was reassigned to the genus Parvicursor by Longrich and Currie in 2008.
facts.quote: IGM 100/99 fue reasignado a Parvicursor por Longrich y Currie en 2008

facts.statement: Mononykus was a member of the family Alvarezsauridae.
facts.quote: Mononykus era un miembro de la familia Alvarezsauridae

facts.statement: Advanced alvarezsaurids including Mononykus, Parvicursor, and Shuvuuia are classified in their own subfamily called Mononykinae.
facts.quote: Posteriormente se encontró Parvicursor, al que también se le asignó su propia familia, Parvicursoridae, y Shuvuia, estos tres alvarezsáuridos avanzados se los clasifica en una propia subfamilia llamada Mononykinae

facts.statement: Mononykus belongs to the group Coelurosauria and has been related to birds.
facts.quote: También se los ha relacionado con las aves, en cualquier caso pertenecen a Coelurosauria

facts.statement: Mononykus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: A 2001 pathological study by Bruce Rothschild and others examined 15 foot bones of Mononykus for stress fractures but found none.
facts.quote: En un estudio patológico realizado en 2001 por Bruce Rothschild y otros paleontólogos, en 15 huesos de un pie de Mononykus el cual fue examinado para detectar signos de fracturas por estrés, pero no encontraron ninguna fractura

facts.statement: In the documentary Prehistoric Planet, Mononykus is depicted with a facial disk similar to owls and a long, sticky tongue for catching termites.
facts.quote: En el documental se la representa con un disco facial similar a las lechuzas y una lengua larga y pegajosa para atrapar termitas

rejected.statement: Although formally described in the 1990s, a specimen possibly belonging to Mononykus was unearthed by the Andrews expedition decades earlier.
rejected.quote: Mononykus was formally described in the 1990s, but it was reported that a specimen possibly belonging to this genus had already been unearthed by the Andrews expedition decades before.
rejected.reason: quote not found verbatim in the source

rejected.statement: Researchers suggest Mononykus may have had a facial disc of specialized feathers similar to owls to help catch sound.
rejected.quote: For this reason it is possible Mononykus also had a facial disc of specialized feathers, similar to extant owls, that served to catch sound and direct it to the ears.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'had a facial disc of specialized feathers similar'

rejected.statement: Specimen AMNH 6524 was found in 1922 by the expedition of Roy Chapman Andrews.
rejected.quote: Encontrado en 1922 por la expedición de Roy Chapman Andrews
